lines.meet: Rhodri, scaffolder back home and the big lump at the front out here. Mind your head on that pole, it's not tied off yet.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're up at Amberwatch too, aren't you? I'm the one hammering on the gatehouse at six in the morning, sorry about that.
lines.ask_home: Where's that accent from, then? I'm guessing nowhere near Pontypridd.
lines.ask_work: What were you before all this? You've got working hands, I noticed straight off.
lines.answer_home: Pontypridd, in the valleys, in South Wales. Terraced streets up the hillsides and a rugby club older than anyone's nan.
lines.answer_work: Scaffolding, with my own van and four lads from my street. Saturdays I propped for Ponty, fifteen seasons in the front row.
lines.chat_food: A pie and a pint after the match, in the clubhouse, with everybody steaming and singing. Nothing on any world beats that.
lines.chat_sleep: Head down and gone, me, like a dropped sack. Up at six whether I like it or not.
lines.chat_missing: I miss Saturdays most. The bus to the away game, the singing on the way home, my nephews on my shoulders at the gate.
lines.chat_here: I woke up on a beach with my boots full of sand and I was carrying poles up a hill by teatime. I didn't know what else to do with myself.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd make a lovely second row, {name}. Head down, mouth shut, shoving like a mule.
lines.tease_talker: Duw, {name}, you could talk the hind legs off a donkey and sell them back to it.
lines.tease_careful: You check things nearly as often as I do, {name}, and I'm the worst for it. We'll get there by Christmas.
lines.tease_bold: You'd run straight at a pack of forwards, you would, {name}. I admire it, but I'd put a helmet on you first.
lines.tease_any: You'd do all right on my crew, {name}, as long as you never touch my ties.
lines.tease_back: Fair play, {name}, that landed. I'll have that one.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ha, you're not wrong, {name}. My mam says the same and she's rarely wrong either.
lines.bristle: Leave that, {name}. There was a young ranger on my scaffold, and I don't joke about it.
lines.needle_quiet: If you see something coming, shout. Standing there silent gets people hurt.
lines.needle_talker: Less talking and more watching, please. Half the trouble out here walks up while somebody's mid-sentence.
lines.needle_careful: At some point you've got to trust the knot and climb. We'll be here all week otherwise.
lines.needle_bold: You keep stepping out of the line, and one day I won't be able to reach you.
lines.needle_any: You never check your straps, and one day that buckle is going to let you down at the worst time.
lines.bite_back: I've stood at the front of every fight we've had. Don't tell me I'm not pulling my weight.
lines.hurt: That one stung, I won't lie. I'll go and put the kettle on and get over it.
lines.laugh_off: I've had seventeen stone of Bridgend forward stood on my head. That barely tickled.
lines.apologise: Sorry, that came out harder than I meant it. I'm tired and you didn't deserve it.
lines.double_down: I'm not taking it back. Somebody needed telling, and I'm the size for it.
lines.confide: {name}, the night the naga came, fire came up through me and I burned one where it stood. What frightens me is how good it felt.
lines.listen: Tell me, {name}, I'm listening, and it goes no further than me.
lines.look_out: Behind me, {name}, and stay there. I'm the wall today.
lines.accept: Fair enough, {name}, your way it is, and I'll hold the door.
lines.deflect: That's nothing, {name}, a lineout's done worse to me. See to somebody else.
lines.check_in: You took a knock there, {name}. Stand still and let's see that strap.
lines.blame: Somebody stepped out of the line and the rest of us paid for it. I felt the gap open.
lines.thank: You had my back there, and that's normally my job. I owe you a pint, a big one.
lines.brush_off: Don't mention it. Standing in the way is what I'm for.
lines.worry: Steady now, {name}, I've got you. Lean on me, I don't fall over.
lines.handed_down: I reckon this was yours. Have it back, it never fitted me anyway.
lines.hand_fine: No bother, take it. I've played in worse kit than this.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody thought of the big fella, then. Right, I'll be over it by teatime.
lines.turn_friendly: Welcome to the crew, {name}, proper. I don't say that to many people.
lines.turn_friends: I'd take any hit going for you, {name}, and I'd let you take one for me, which is harder.
lines.turn_grating: We grate on each other, us two, there's no hiding it. No matter, the job still gets done.
lines.turn_rivals: If you're face down in the mud I'll still drag you out. Don't expect a pint after.
lines.make_up: Come on, {name}, let's knock this on the head. Shake on it and start again?
lines.defend: Oi, leave off, that's not on. {name} held their end up all day.
lines.friend_left: The crew's a man short without {name}, and I keep turning round to say something.
lines.friend_back: There they are! {name}'s back and the crew's whole again, lovely.
lines.common_welsh: A Welsh voice, out here! Where are you from, then? Tell me it's somewhere I've played.
lines.common_sport: You played, didn't you? You've got the look. Every team I was ever on had somebody who stood like that.
lines.common_craft: You've built things with your hands, I can tell. Anybody who's made something properly knows you check it twice.
